newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Representative Joker Arroyo says Malacanang is conspiring with the Commission on Elections in orchestrating the signature campaign for constitutional amendments, as Pirma says it will continue to gather signature to amend the Constitution. (ALL PAPERS)
- A suspected extortionist, whose detention is believed to have led to the killing of Sulu Bishop Benjamin de Jesus, escaped from the Jolo Municipal Jail with six other inmates. (TODAY)
- Defense secretary Renato de Villa says his being a former soldier should not be viewed as a negative factor in his bid for the presidency. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Economists say they are alarmed by the rise in car imports saying the market is already saturated. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Philippines has drummed up support from members of the World Trade Organisation against the imposition by the United States of the new rule of origin on garment exports (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The liberalisation of retail trade in the country will yield a hefty 5.4 billion pesos in additional income for the government each year, a study by the Department of Finance says. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- A local subsidiary of TDK Corp is investing 18.31 billion pesos over the next five years to put up a manufacturing plant for components of computer hard disk drives.
